subject: toad fly
title: This Fly's Maggots Eat Living Toads From the Nose Inward

scenes.text: A fly can kill a toad without ever biting it.
It's called the toad fly, and across Europe it targets living common toads.
It lays its eggs right on the toad's skin, often near the nostrils and eyes.
The maggots crawl into the nose and start eating the toad's head from the inside.
Infected toads stop hiding and sit out in the open. That invites even more flies.
Within a week, it's dead. Killed by a fly that never bit it once.

description:
A fly can kill a common toad without ever biting it.
The toad fly, Lucilia bufonivora, lays eggs on living toads, often around the nostrils and eyes. The maggots move into the nose and feed on the living head. Infected toads sit out in the open, and they die within a few days to a week. There is no cure.
Have you ever seen a toad with a damaged nose?
first_comment: A 2022 study found toad fly infections in 12 European countries, mostly in bigger, older female toads. Would you rather be the toad or the fly?
